header.running_head: Reprimanding those who Occupy Themselves with Learning Things that are Contrary to that Which Rasulullaah ﷺ Taught

blocks.text: never allow yourselves to be deceived by the confused ones (the Ahlul Kitaab).'"

Hadhrat Umar (RA) continues, "I then stood up and said, 'I am satisfied with Allaah as my Rabb, with Islaam as my religion and with you as my Nabi.' Rasulullaah ﷺ then descended from the pulpit." [^1]

Hadhrat Jaabir (RA) narrates that Hadhrat Umar bin Khattaab (RA) once brought to Rasulullaah ﷺ a scripture that he got from some people of the Ahlul Kitaab. "O Rasulullaah ﷺ!" he said, "I just got an excellent scripture from some people of the Ahlul Kitaab." Rasulullaah ﷺ became angry and said, "Are you people in doubt, O son of Khattaab? I swear by the Being Who controls my life! What I have brought to you is clear and pure. You therefore have no need to ask them. (The danger is that) They might tell you some truth that you may reject or tell you some false that you may believe. I swear by the Being Who controls my life that even if Moosa (AS) was alive, he would have no option but to follow me." [^2]

Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Thaabit (RA) narrates that Hadhrat Umar bin Khattaab (RA) once came to Rasulullaah ﷺ and said, "I was passing by a friend from the (Jewish) Banu Qurayzah tribe, so he wrote down for me some quotations from the Torah. Should I read them to you." When Rasulullaah ﷺ's face started reddening (with anger), Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Thaabit (RA) said to Hadhrat Umar (RA), "Can you not see Rasulullaah ﷺ's face?" Hadhrat Umar (RA) immediately exclaimed, "I am satisfied with Allaah as my Rabb, with Islaam as my religion and with Muhammad ﷺ as my Nabi." Rasulullaah ﷺ's anger then subsided and he said, "I swear by the Being Who controls the life of Muhammad! If Moosa (AS) had to be amongst you and you leave me to follow him, you would certainly go astray. You are meant to be my Ummah and I am meant to be your Nabi." [^3]
Hadhrat Umar (RA) Rebukes a man who told him That he Found a Scripture with wonderful Content

Hadhrat Maymoon bin Mahraan narrates that a man came to Hadhrat Umar (RA) saying, "O Ameerul Mu'mineen! When we conquered Madaa'in, I found a scripture with wonderful content." "Is the content consistent with the Book of Allaah?" Hadhrat Umar (RA) asked. When the man said that it was not, Hadhrat Umar (RA) sent for his whip, lashed the man and recited the verse:

blocks.arabic_text: الٓرٰ ۚ تِلْكَ اٰيٰتُ الْكِتٰبِ الْمُبِيْنِ ۝ إِنَّآ أَنْزَلْنٰهُ قُرْءٰنًا عَرَبِيًّا لَّعَلَّكُمْ تَعْقِلُوْنَ ۝

blocks.text: Abu Ya'la. Haythami (Vol.1 Pg.182) has commented on the chain of narrators. Ibnul Mundhir, Ibn Abi Haatim, Uqayli, Nasr Maqdasi, Sa'eed bin Mansoor and Abdur Razzaaq have reported a similar narration, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.1 Pg.94).
Ibn Abdul Birr in his Jaami (Vol.2 Pg.42). Ahmad, Abu Ya'la and Bazzaar have reported a similar narration but Haythami (Vol.1 Pg.174) has commented on the chain of narrators.
